name: French (Classical & Bistro)
description: Emphasizes mirepoix aromatics, cultured butter and cream emulsions, wine and stock reductions, fine herbs (tarragon, chervil, thyme, parsley), and structured acid-fat balance.
flavorStructureNotes: Builds deep savory foundations through browned proteins and alliums, enriched with dairy or duck fat and lifted at the finish with wine, vinegar, or fresh herbs.

name: Italian (Regional Peninsula & Islands)
description: Spans Northern butter/rice/polenta traditions to Central/Southern olive oil, tomato, hard aged cheeses, bitter greens, and coastal seafood preparations.
flavorStructureNotes: Relies on high-quality primary ingredients, glutamates from aged cheese, cured pork, or anchovies, and bright acidity from tomatoes, wine, or citrus.

name: Spanish & Western Mediterranean
description: Anchored by olive oil, garlic, smoked paprika (pimentón), saffron, sherry vinegar, almonds, legumes, chorizo, and coastal shellfish.
flavorStructureNotes: Pairs smoky, nutty, and saffron-infused aromatics with sharp sherry vinegar acidity and rich olive oil emulsions.

name: Mexican (Central, Oaxacan & Coastal)
description: Built on nixtamalized corn, diverse fresh and dried chiles, tomatillos, tomatoes, lime, cilantro, epazote, pumpkin seeds, avocado, and complex toasted spice/seed moles.
flavorStructureNotes: Balances earthy roasted chiles and toasted seeds/nuts with bright fresh lime, raw onion/cilantro, and creamy avocado or queso fresco.

name: Japanese (Washoku & Izakaya)
description: Focused on dashi umami (kombu and katsuobushi), fermented soy (shoyu, miso), mirin, rice vinegar, ginger, scallions, sesame, and seasonal precision.
flavorStructureNotes: Layers clean synergistic umami (glutamate + inosinate) with gentle sweetness from mirin and delicate acidity from rice vinegar or yuzu/citrus.

name: Chinese (Sichuan & Southwestern)
description: Renowned for compound flavor profiles (yu xiang, ma la, guai wei) combining fermented broad bean paste (doubanjiang), Sichuan peppercorn, ginger, garlic, scallion, black vinegar, and chili oil.
flavorStructureNotes: Orchestrates numbing citrus-floral notes (Sichuan peppercorn), fiery heat, fermented savory depth, sugar, and aged black vinegar into multi-layered profiles.

name: Chinese (Cantonese & Coastal Southern)
description: Prioritizes ingredient freshness, wok hei (breath of the wok), gentle steaming, ginger-scallion aromatics, oyster sauce, Shaoxing wine, and clear savory broths.
flavorStructureNotes: Highlights natural sweetness of seafood, poultry, and greens using light aromatic infusions and savory umami glazes that never mask the main component.

name: Korean
description: Grounded in fermented jang pastes (gochujang, doenjang), ganjang (soy sauce), garlic, ginger, gochugaru, toasted sesame oil, perilla, and vibrant fermented kimchi accompaniments.
flavorStructureNotes: Contrasts deep fermented earthiness and chili warmth with crisp pickled/fermented vegetables, toasted sesame richness, and fruit-sweetened marinades.

name: Indian (Northern & Mughlai)
description: Characterized by whole and ground warming spices (cumin, coriander, cardamom, cinnamon, cloves), onion-ginger-garlic-tomato bhuna foundations, ghee, yogurt, cream, and tandoor roasting.
flavorStructureNotes: Blooms fat-soluble spices in hot ghee or oil (tadka), layers caramelized onions and ginger-garlic, and balances spice heat with cultured dairy or tangy chutney.

name: Indian (Southern & Coastal)
description: Built around coconut, curry leaves, black mustard seeds, tamarind, black pepper, lentils, fermented rice-lentil batters, and vibrant coastal seafood and vegetable preparations.
flavorStructureNotes: Pairs pungent tempered mustard seeds and aromatic curry leaves with sharp sour tamarind and cooling, rich coconut milk.

name: Thai (Central & Regional)
description: Famous for the dynamic four-corner equilibrium of salty (fish sauce), sour (lime, tamarind), sweet (palm sugar), and spicy (fresh chiles), perfumed with lemongrass, galangal, makrut lime leaf, and Thai basil.
flavorStructureNotes: Demands simultaneous high-intensity contrast: pungent umami fish sauce, sharp citrus/tamarind acidity, aromatic herbs, chile heat, and palm sugar.

name: Vietnamese
description: Emphasizes fresh raw table herbs (mint, cilantro, Thai basil, perilla), nuoc mam (fish sauce), lime, rice noodles/paper, charred meats, and crystal-clear spiced broths.
flavorStructureNotes: Uses minimal added fat, relying on bright sweet-sour-savory nuoc cham, crisp pickled vegetables, and abundant fresh herbs to cut rich grilled or braised proteins.

name: Middle Eastern & Levantine
description: Features tahini (sesame paste), sumac, za'atar, pomegranate molasses, lemon, garlic, olive oil, chickpeas, eggplant, lamb, yogurt, and warm spices (allspice, cumin, cinnamon).
flavorStructureNotes: Combines earthy sesame/nut richness and charred vegetables or meats with bright floral-tart acidity from sumac, lemon, and pomegranate.

name: North African (Maghrebi)
description: Signature slow-cooked tagines combining preserved lemon, green olives, harissa, cumin, coriander, ginger, saffron, cinnamon, honey, dried fruits, almonds, and couscous.
flavorStructureNotes: Weaves savory-sweet-sour harmony: aromatic warm spices and honey/dried fruit sweetness counterbalanced by briny preserved lemon, olives, and fiery harissa.

name: West African & Caribbean Diaspora
description: Connects West African groundnut (peanut), tomato-chili-ginger stews, plantains, yams, and leafy greens with Caribbean allspice (pimento), Scotch bonnet/habanero, thyme, lime, and coconut.
flavorStructureNotes: Balances high aromatic chile heat and pungent ginger/allspice with creamy peanut or coconut richness and sweet starchy plantains or tubers.
